commit_message:
lavc/vvc: Add max parameter to kth_order_egk_decode

Prior to this patch, kth_order_egk_decode could read arbitrarily
large values which then overflowed and caused various issues.
Patch fixes this by making kth_order_egk_decode falliable,
requiring the caller to specify an upper bound and returning an
error if the read value would exceed that bound.

This patch resolves the same issue as
eb52251c0ab025b6b40b28994bc9dc616813b190, but I think this is the proper
fix as it also addresses issues with syntax elements besides
ff_vvc_num_signalled_palette_entries.

Signed-off-by: Frank Plowman <post@frankplowman.com>

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/vvc/ctu: check coeff before multiply

ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() can return AVERROR in which case the
coeff*scale will overflow.

Fixes: runtime error: signed integer overflow: -1094995529 * 6528 cannot
       be represented in type 'int'
Fixes: 435225406/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_VVC_fuzzer-5118570024730624
Found-by: OSS-Fuzz
Signed-off-by: Kacper Michajłow <kasper93@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 75f30b4d3e23 on top of intro 7c5319e6924f via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): In FFmpeg's VVC (H.266) decoder, palette_subblock_data() in libavcodec/vvc/ctu.c decodes escape-coded palette entries by calling ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() to read a coefficient value from the bitstream, then computes pixel = av_clip_intp2(RSHIFT(coeff * scale, 6), bit_depth). ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() can return a negative AVERROR code (e.g. AVERROR_INVALIDDATA, a large negative int) if the bounded k-th order Exp-Golomb decode fails validation against the maximum allowed value. Because the code multiplied 'coeff' by 'scale' before checking whether 'coeff' was negative/an error code, a crafted bitstream could trigger a large negative coeff which, multiplied by scale, causes signed integer overflow (undefined behavior in C, detected by UBSan/OSS-Fuzz). Root cause: When ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() was made failable (returning negative AVERROR codes) as part of a broader refactor to bound Exp-Golomb decoding, the caller in palette_subblock_data() was updated to check the new error condition, but the validation check ('if (coeff < 0) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;') was placed after the arithmetic expression that uses 'coeff' in a multiplication, rather than before it. This ordering mistake allowed the invalid/error sentinel value to participate in signed multiplication, causing overflow.
